name: OECD.AI Policy Observatory: national AI policies, data and principles
title: OECD.AI Policy Observatory: national AI policies, data and principles
answer: OECD.AI is the OECD Artificial Intelligence Policy Observatory. This landing page says it provides access to more than 900 national AI policies and initiatives, live data about AI, and a blog about AI policy. It also describes the OECD AI Principles for trustworthy AI and a July 2024 integrated partnership between the GPAI initiative and OECD member countries' work on AI. For government readers, its main value is as a pointer to a broad policy observatory rather than a detailed account of any single policy.

sections.body: This is the landing page for OECD.AI, the OECD Artificial Intelligence Policy Observatory. The text presents it as a source of access to national AI policies and initiatives, live data about AI, and a blog about AI policy. It also refers to the OECD AI Principles and to a July 2024 integrated partnership between the GPAI initiative and OECD member countries' work on AI. The page is short and overview level, and it does not state a separate publication date for itself.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The source says OECD.AI helps countries and shape trustworthy AI with the OECD AI Principles. It gives access to 900+ national AI policies and initiatives, live data about AI and a blog about AI policy. It states that organisations developing advanced AI systems can participate by submitting a report. By sharing information, they will facilitate transparency and comparability of risk mitigation measures. It says the GPAI initiative and OECD member countries' work on AI joined forces under the GPAI brand to create an integrated partnership. It dates this to July 2024 and invites readers to find out more. It also states that the aim is to help AI actors develop and use trustworthy AI systems and applications that respect human rights and are fair, transparent, explainable, robust, secure and safe. The page does not describe individual national policies, nor does it explain how the 900+ policies and initiatives are collected or updated. It functions as an entry point to the observatory rather than a detailed policy analysis.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that OECD.AI gives access to 900+ national AI policies and initiatives. It states that the GPAI initiative and OECD member countries' work on AI joined forces under the GPAI brand in July 2024 to create an integrated partnership. It states that organisations developing advanced AI systems can participate by submitting a report, which it says will facilitate transparency and comparability of risk mitigation measures. It lists the qualities sought for trustworthy AI systems and applications as respecting human rights and being fair, transparent, explainable, robust, secure and safe. It gives no other figures.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Government can use this source as a signpost to a large collection of national AI policies and initiatives, live AI data and policy commentary. It is useful for orientation, for seeing that an observatory exists and for finding the OECD AI Principles and the GPAI partnership. It does not provide a government case study, procurement guidance or implementation detail. Its value is in pointing to where policy material may be found, not in explaining how any specific government has adopted or regulated AI.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Government

sections.body: This is a short landing page, not a full report or dataset. It does not list the 900+ policies and initiatives, does not describe their contents, and does not explain how they are selected or updated. It gives no methodology, no country-by-country findings and no implementation examples. It mentions July 2024 for the GPAI partnership but does not date the page itself. It is therefore partial and best used as a starting point, with the underlying observatory needed for detail.
